title: Who Wrote Boomer Sooner? The 1905 Origin of OU's Fight Song
question: Who wrote the Boomer Sooner fight song and where does the tune come from?
answer: OU student Arthur M. Alden wrote the words to "Boomer Sooner" in 1905, setting them to the tune of Yale's "Boola Boola." A year later a section borrowed from North Carolina's "I'm a Tar Heel Born" was added.
summary: Boomer Sooner began in 1905 when OU student Arthur M. Alden put words to Yale's Boola Boola tune. A Tar Heel addition came in 1906. Here's the full story.
body: It may be the most played song in Norman, and it started with a student. In 1905 Arthur M. Alden, who studied history and physiology and whose father was a Norman jeweler, wrote the lyrics that became "Boomer Sooner." He did not write a new melody. Instead he borrowed the tune of Yale's "Boola Boola" and fit his own words to it.

That Yale tune has its own backstory. It traces to "La Hoola Boola," an 1898 song by Bob Cole and Billy Johnson, which Yale adapted into its famous cheer. So when Sooner fans sing their fight song, they are carrying a little piece of turn-of-the-century American popular music along with them.

The song grew a year later. In 1906 a section borrowed from the University of North Carolina's "I'm a Tar Heel Born" was added, and the two pieces were combined into the fight song fans know today. That is why the familiar line about being Sooner born and Sooner bred sounds so close to the Carolina original.

The lyrics are famously simple, built mostly on repeating the two Land Run words, Boomer and Sooner, along with Oklahoma and OU. That simplicity is part of the appeal. Fans have informally counted the Pride of Oklahoma playing it dozens of times in a single game, and it has become one of the most recognizable fight songs in the country.
